arxiv-1907-13508.title: Evolutionary Dataset Optimisation: learning algorithm quality through evolution
arxiv-1907-13508.creator: Henry Wilde, Vincent Knight, Jonathan Gillard
arxiv-1907-13508.description: Abstract In this paper we propose a novel method for learning how algorithms perform. Classically, algorithms are compared on a finite number of existing (or newly simulated) benchmark datasets based on some fixed metrics. The algorithm(s) with the smallest value of this metric are chosen to be the ‘best performing’. We offer a new approach to flip this paradigm.

arxiv-2102-12653.title: An Errata for: Torsion subgroups of rational elliptic curves over the compositum of all D 4 D_{4} extensions of the rational numbers
arxiv-2102-12653.creator: Harris B. Daniels
arxiv-2102-12653.description: Abstract . In [ 2 ] , the author claims that the fields ℚ ⁡ ( D 4 ∞ ) \mathbb{Q}(D_{4}^{\infty}) defined in the paper and the compositum of all D 4 D_{4} extensions of ℚ \mathbb{Q} coincide. The proof of this claim depends on a misreading of a celebrated result by Shafarevich.

arxiv-2304-11757.title: Computing Controlled Invariant Sets of Nonlinear Control-Affine Systems
arxiv-2304-11757.creator: Scott Brown, Mohammad Khajenejad, Sze Zheng Yong, Sonia Martínez
arxiv-2304-11757.description: Abstract In this paper, we consider the computation of controlled invariant sets (CIS) of discrete-time nonlinear control-affine systems. We propose an iterative refinement procedure based on polytopic inclusion functions, which is able to approximate the maximal controlled invariant set to within a guaranteed precision.

arxiv-2312-03953.title: Norm convergence of confined fermionic systems at zero temperature
arxiv-2312-03953.creator: Esteban Cárdenas
arxiv-2312-03953.description: Abstract . The semi-classical limit of ground states of large systems of fermions was studied by Fournais, Lewin and Solovej in (Calc. Var. Partial Differ. Equ., 2018). In particular, the authors prove weak convergence towards classical states associated to the minimizers of the Thomas-Fermi functional.

arxiv-2402-02653.title: Learning with Mixture of Prototypes for Out-of-Distribution Detection
arxiv-2402-02653.creator: Haodong Lu, Dong Gong, Shuo Wang, Jason Xue, Lina Yao, Kristen Moore
arxiv-2402-02653.description: Abstract Out-of-distribution (OOD) detection aims to detect testing samples far away from the in-distribution (ID) training data, which is crucial for the safe deployment of machine learning models in the real world. Distance-based OOD detection methods have emerged with enhanced deep representation learning. They identify unseen OOD samples by measuring their distances from ID class centroids or prototypes.

arxiv-2405-07235.title: Does gravitational wave assist vacuum steering and Bell nonlocality?
arxiv-2405-07235.creator: Shu-Min Wu 1 , Rui-Di Wang 1 , Xiao-Li Huang 1 , Zejun Wang 2
arxiv-2405-07235.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shu-Min Wu 1 , Rui-Di Wang 1 , Xiao-Li Huang 1 , Zejun Wang 2. We study quantum steering and Bell nonlocality harvested by the local interaction of two Unruh-DeWitt detectors with the vacuum massless scalar field, both in the presence of gravitational waves and in Minkowski spacetime.

arxiv-2407-04654.title: Metastability of the contact process on slowly evolving scale-free networks
arxiv-2407-04654.creator: Emmanuel Jacob, Amitai Linker and Peter Mörters
arxiv-2407-04654.description: Abstract Abstract: We investigate the contact process on scale-free networks evolving by a stationary dynamics whereby each vertex independently updates its connections with a rate depending on its power. This rate can be slowed down or speeded up by virtue of decreasing or increasing a parameter \eta , with \eta\downarrow-\infty approaching the static and \eta\uparrow\infty the mean-field case.

arxiv-2407-12882.title: InstructAV: Instruction Fine-tuning Large Language Models for Authorship Verification
arxiv-2407-12882.creator: Yujia Hu, Zhiqiang Hu, Chun-Wei Seah, Roy Ka-Wei Lee
arxiv-2407-12882.description: Abstract Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated remarkable proficiency in a wide range of NLP tasks. However, when it comes to authorship verification (AV) tasks, which involve determining whether two given texts share the same authorship, even advanced models like ChatGPT exhibit notable limitations. This paper introduces a novel approach, termed InstructAV , for authorship verification.

arxiv-2507-15495.title: Thin-shell bounds via parallel coupling
arxiv-2507-15495.creator: Boaz Klartag, Joseph Lehec
arxiv-2507-15495.description: Abstract We prove that for any log-concave random vector X X in ℝ n \mathbb{R}^{n} with mean zero and identity covariance, 𝔼 ​ ( | X | − n ) 2 ≤ C \mathbb{E}(|X|-\sqrt{n})^{2}\leq C (91) where C > 0 C>0 is a universal constant.

arxiv-2510-08901.title: Modeling Time-Lapse Trajectories to Characterize Cranberry Growth
arxiv-2510-08901.creator: Ronan John Anis Chihoub Ryan Meegan Gina Sidelli Jeffery Neyhart Peter Oudemans Kristin Dana
arxiv-2510-08901.description: Abstract Change monitoring is an essential task for cranberry farming as it provides both breeders and growers with the ability to analyze growth, predict yield, and make treatment decisions. However, this task is often done manually, requiring significant time on the part of a cranberry grower or breeder.

arxiv-2604-07140.title: Symmetry-Engineered Magnetic Dipole Emission in Plasmonic Core–Satellite Resonators
arxiv-2604-07140.creator: Joshua Davis, Sébastien Bidault, Mathieu Mivelle, Mona Tréguer-Delapierre, Alexandre Baron

europmc-pmc3389649.title: The development and immunosuppressive functions of CD4(+) CD25(+) FoxP3(+) regulatory T cells are under influence of the adenosine-A2A adenosine receptor pathway.
europmc-pmc3389649.creator: Ohta A, Kini R, Ohta A, Subramanian M, Madasu M, Sitkovsky M.
europmc-pmc3389649.description: The A2A adenosine receptor (A2AR)-mediated immunosuppression is firmly implicated in the life-saving down-regulation of collateral tissue damage during the anti-pathogen immune response and in highly undesirable protection of cancerous tissues during anti-tumor immune response....

pmc-10552851.title: Sustainable collaboration on complex problems: a “who” not a “what” challenge
pmc-10552851.creator: Josie Gibson
pmc-10552851.description: Despite decades of collective efforts and millions of dollars of cross-sector investment, collaborations created to address wicked problems—complex issues that span industries and sectors whose root causes are unclear—have had mixed success. The wicked problems terrain is tribal and competitive.

pmc-10567532.title: Medical Management of Chronic Subdural Hematoma
pmc-10567532.creator: Kyung Hwan Kim, Young Lee
pmc-10567532.description: Chronic subdural hematoma (CSDH) is a commonly encountered disease in the field of neurosurgery, typically resulting from head trauma. Several medical treatments have been introduced to manage patients with CSDH though surgical drainage is the main strategy to manage symptomatic patients. This review is aimed to meticulously examine contemporary pharmacological approaches, based on a thorough understanding of CSDH pathophysiology.

pmc-10595380.title: The mental health of children and adolescents at Matosinhos: characteristics and obstacles to care
pmc-10595380.creator: R Barbabela, G Duarte, T Leão
pmc-10595380.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). BackgroundMental health disorders are a public health issue. Most mental disorders begin during childhood and adolescence. Epidemiological studies regarding the diagnosis, prevalence, and access to treatment by children and adolescents are scarce, especially in Portugal.

pmc-10713388.title: Pyogenic Spondylitis Caused by Parvimonas micra: A Case Report
pmc-10713388.creator: Saneyuki Itagaki, Tsuneaki Kenzaka
pmc-10713388.description: Parvimonas micra (P. micra) is a gram-positive anaerobic coccus endemic to the oral cavity and intestinal tract. We report a case of pyogenic spondylitis caused by P. micra and summarize the clinical features of previous case reports. An 81-year-old man with a history of lumbar vertebral compression fracture two years previously presented to the emergency department with low back pain.

pmc-12361516.title: Dynamic land-cover maps in the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area at 30 m spatial resolution, 2000-2022
pmc-12361516.creator: Yue Li, Qiang Liu, Shuang Chen, Lingfeng Lv, Xinpei Han, Run Jia, Lingchen Bu, Xiaotong Zhang
pmc-12361516.description: As a world-class urban agglomeration, the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area (GBA) has experienced substantial land-cover restructuring driven by urbanization, necessitating high temporal resolution monitoring to capture dynamic surface processes. However, traditional land-cover products cannot capture intra-annual dynamics effectively due to their limited update cycles.

pmc-12403355.title: The positive impact of students in general practice clerkships in rural Germany: diverging views of students, general practitioners, and practice assistants in a prospective survey
pmc-12403355.creator: Wolfgang Blank, Anna Sporkert, Lars Daenenfaust, Sabine Gehrke-Beck
pmc-12403355.description: BackgroundRecruiting and retention of teaching practices is challenging. Although GP teaching physicians are predominantly intrinsically motivated, the time required for teaching is often cited as a barrier. Practice teams could benefit, if the students’ learning in practice is optimized in such a way that there is also a noticeable positive impact in daily work.

pmc-12819208.title: The relationship between college students’ perceived physical education environment and student engagement: a latent profile and structural equation modeling analysis
pmc-12819208.creator: Anlin Guan, Liguo Zhang, Huizhuo Wu
pmc-12819208.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundCollege students’ participation in physical education (PE) classes is of great significance to teaching effectiveness and students’ physical and mental health. However, few studies have explored the influencing factors and mechanisms of PE class engagement. This study aims to investigate the association between college students’ perceived PE environment and their PE class engagement, as well as the mediating roles of perceived teacher support and academic self-efficacy.MethodsA cross-sectional survey was conducted among 1,158 Chinese college students from December 1 to 31, 2024.

pmc-13051717.title: Associations between various lipid indices and coronary collateral circulation in patients with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a cross-sectional study
pmc-13051717.creator: Tianfeng Zhang, Chenghua Wang, Zhenghui Wang, Long Zhao, Hao Xia, Yiming Wang, Chunyang Yin
pmc-13051717.description: BackgroundThis study aims to evaluate the association between multiple lipid indices and coronary collateral circulation (CCC) in patients diagnosed with acute ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).MethodsThis was a cross-sectional retrospective study involving 421 patients with STEMI who underwent coronary angiography between January 2022 and December 2024.

pmc-13203059.title: Effects of fecal microbiota transplantation and probiotics on the gut microbiome in antibiotic-treated septic patients: A pilot randomized controlled trial
pmc-13203059.creator: Yuanzhuo Chen, Jian Zhao, Jiangman Zhao, Qiyi Chen, Shi Dong, Shaohua Jia, Yi Zhao, Di Hao, Yangyang Yin, Sitong Lin, Yanqing Chen, Yugang Zhuang, Hu Peng
pmc-13203059.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Broad-spectrum antibiotics, essential for sepsis management in critically ill patients, cause significant gut dysbiosis. Restoring gut microbiota may improve outcomes, but the efficacy of interventions like fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) and probiotics in this setting remains underexplored. This study aims to evaluate the feasibility and potential efficacy of FMT versus probiotics on gut microbiome restoration and inflammatory markers in critically ill, antibiotic-treated sepsis patients.

pmc-13311297.title: Comparative Effectiveness of Massage Gun and Myofascial Release Technique for Releasing Latent Trigger Points of Calf Muscle: A Randomized Clinical Trial
pmc-13311297.creator: Md Mafrohi Sattar, Abid Hasan Khan, Kazi Md Azman Hossain, Md Feroz Kabir, Sharmila Jahan, K M Amran Hossain, Ehsanur Rahman, Farzana Sharmin, Md Saruar Hossain Bhuiyan, Azharul Islam, Md Kabir Hossain, Md Zahid Hossain

pmc-13330524.title: High-throughput, multiplex immunofluorescence for the computer-automated immunophenotyping of Mycosis Fungoides
pmc-13330524.creator: Patrick McMullan, Marc R Benoit, Nathan Gasek, Sydney Riddick, Joseph Masison, Katalin Ferenczi, David Rowe, Gillian Weston
pmc-13330524.description: The diagnosis of mycosis fungoides is difficult and often delayed, exacerbated by the limitation of conventional immunohistochemistry to analyze only 1 antigen per tissue section, often necessitating repeat biopsies and extensive workups. We sought to validate a high-throughput multiplex immunofluorescence method, coupled with computer-automated image analysis, to generate comprehensive immunophenotyping data from a single formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded biopsy.

pmc-13331556.title: A microscopically assisted limited colectomy mouse model of early colon cancer
pmc-13331556.creator: Yu Han, Yixin Zhang, Dazhi Gao, Xuefeng Zhao
pmc-13331556.description: BackgroundCurrently, there is a lack of an adequate rodent model for investigating surgical techniques and comprehensive treatment options for patients with colorectal cancer (CRC). This study presents a mouse model that involves the orthotopic implantation of colon cancer, followed by a limited colectomy, with the aim of addressing this issue.

pmc-13359424.title: Barriers and facilitators to implementing e-learning for infection management in primary care: a scoping review
pmc-13359424.creator: Louise Bidstrup Jørgensen, Jette Nygaard Jensen, Caroline Skovsbo Clausen, Marius Brostrøm Kousgaard, Sif Helene Arnold
pmc-13359424.description: BackgroundInfections are among the most common reasons for consultations in primary care, and appropriate infection management is essential to patient safety and antimicrobial stewardship. Educational interventions can improve diagnostic and prescribing practices, but in-person training is resource-intensive and difficult to scale. E-learning offers a flexible alternative; however, little is known about factors that influence its implementation in primary care.

pmc-13389443.title: Evaluating the Toxicity and Safety of Turmeric (Curcuma longa L.) and Its Components: A Narrative Review
pmc-13389443.creator: Jalileh Jalali, Mahboobeh Ghasemzadeh Rahbardar
pmc-13389443.description: Turmeric (Curcuma longa), a widely used botanical in traditional medicine, has gained global attention for its therapeutic potential, particularly due to its components including curcumin. While its pharmacological benefits are extensively documented, concerns regarding its safety profile and potential toxicity have emerged, especially with high‐dose supplementation and long‐term use.

pmc-13540846.title: Assessing aflatoxin knowledge, perceptions, and related practices, in a rural coastal community: a population-based cross-sectional survey
pmc-13540846.creator: Rosebella Iseme-Ondiek, Joseph Abuodha, Anthony Ngugi, Innocent Abayo, Mansoor Saleh

pmc-13572106.title: Primary healthcare professionals’ perspectives on mobility limitation assessment and predictive model optimization for community-dwelling older adults: a qualitative research
pmc-13572106.creator: Linbing Chen, Ye Ouyang, Chunyu Cheng, Xiyi Liu, Yanfei Xiang, Liping Wang
pmc-13572106.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundMobility limitation is an important public health challenge faced by ageing populations. However, standardized assessment tools remain lacking in primary care practice in China, and existing predictive models still face substantial implementation gaps in clinical translation. This qualitative study aimed to explore frontline primary healthcare professionals’ perceptions of current assessment practices and to provide recommendations for optimizing and clinically translating related predictive models.MethodsA descriptive qualitative study was conducted in January 2026 among 15 frontline primary healthcare professionals in Dongguan City, China.
